quote: I have a question for you before you even get started. Do you all do solars on townhouses?
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a specific, motivated question before the rep even runs the intro fully — this is a strong receptivity signal the rep could have anchored on ('great question, that's exactly why I called') rather than moving straight into verify-mode.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to name and reflect unsolicited customer questions back before diving into qualification — it builds rapport and signals the call is being driven by the customer's interest, not a script.

quote: Now that, I have to ask Ernest because he is the one staying in it right now.
stewart_read: The actual bill-payer/resident is a third co-owner not on this call. Reactive read: rep should have paused qualification and asked directly whether Ernest could be reached or added to the call. Strategic read is weak here — the rep does wait passively rather than actively working to get Ernest on the line or scheduling around his availability.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic patience — rep may have judged that pushing too hard for Ernest mid-call would frustrate the sister and cost the lead entirely.
coaching_implication: When the qualifying resident/co-owner is absent, the rep should proactively ask for a callback time when Ernest IS available, rather than letting the sister free-solo search for old bills.

quote: My husband used to help take care of my mom's, the cove bill, he said, was around about 140.
stewart_read: This $140 figure is secondhand, admittedly recalled from a different context ('my mom's... the cove bill'), and is not confirmed as the actual current bill for the townhouse in question. It should be treated as low-confidence, unverified data rather than a clean bill capture; coaching a flip on this number would risk anchoring the pitch to the wrong household's expense.
coaching_implication: Flag for the rep: distinguish between a verified current bill and a secondhand approximation. If using an unverified number, note it explicitly as provisional rather than treating it as the anchor.

quote: do you have a credit score over 6 70 for any all three of you?
stewart_read: With three co-owners on title, the rep asks a compound question ('for any all three of you') that doesn't cleanly resolve whether all three need to individually qualify or just one. This isn't a defined protocol violation — the schema's protocols section doesn't cover multi-owner credit scenarios — it's a verify-precision gap where the qualifying question wasn effectively answered before the rep moved on.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have intentionally kept the question loose since only one owner's answer ('Well, I do. Yeah.') was needed to pass the gate, treating any qualifying owner as sufficient.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly clarify the credit qualifier rule for multi-owner properties — does one qualifying owner suffice, or do all title-holders need to clear 670? This ambiguity should be resolved with Kenny and then asked cleanly on calls like this.

quote: When when my mom passed away, they Oh, Oh, I'm sorry.
stewart_read: A reference to a mother's passing appears mid-transcript during the paperwork search. Speaker attribution around this segment is ambiguous in the transcript (the 'Oh, I'm sorry' may be the customer reacting to her own words rather than the rep responding) — this needs audio review before being used as a confirmed rep-empathy-miss in coaching.
alternative_hypothesis: The 'Oh, I'm sorry' could be the customer's own self-interruption rather than the rep's response, in which case there is no empathy miss to coach.
coaching_implication: Do not coach this as a confirmed miss without listening to the audio to confirm who says 'Oh, I'm sorry' at 05:32. If it is the customer talking to herself, this entry should be disregarded.

quote: I sent you a text, and then you can just send a picture of that back. And then I'll call you back whenever, and then I'll schedule you. Okay?
stewart_read: The call ends with a vague future callback ('whenever') instead of a locked day/time or even a specific callback window. There is no 'is that fair?' handshake and no hour-block or no-driving framing since no appointment was actually set.
coaching_implication: Even when bill data isn't available live, the rep should lock a specific callback day/time window ('I'll call you back Thursday around 2 once you've had a chance to reach Ernest') rather than leaving it open-ended.
